summary: {LEVEL} is held from the week before the alarm. It does not come from any week ahead being unusually high. The drift latch has been set since {LATCHED} after a downward breach, so all forecasts are untrusted until a person approves a latch reset. Attendances fell from {F1} to {F2} and then to {F3}, so look at the released weeks rather than any forecast.
expected_range: No forecast range can be trusted while the drift latch is set, so this brief gives no range to plan within for the weeks from {WEEK1} to {WEEK4}.
model_agreement: All forecasts are untrusted while the drift latch is set. This brief names no model to trust less and offers no forecast as a basis for planning. The back-test error in this brief is historical and does not override the latch.
watch_points: Compare the released weeks up to {ORIGIN} with the rota already set, and note how far attendances have fallen below the usual.
Hold any decision to release extra shifts or bank staff until attendances in the latest released weeks are checked.

Ask for the latch to be reviewed; a person approves a latch reset once the documented reset criteria are met. Review the rota after the next data release, and keep the forecasts out of planning while the latch is set.
